1418.label: the held-out authority gate
1418.n_note: 1,418 is the number of VECTORS in the pinned query cache, and it is the instrument's name in every ruling and every sealed arm, so it does not move. It was never the number of scored rows: the battery scores 1,396 rows since ADR-107 amendment 3 (1,420 before it), of which 1,065 carry golds (1,089 before it). The cache is a query->vector lookup table and the scorer iterates ROWS, so a removed row's vector is inert; it is left in the cache on purpose, because every surviving query then keeps the byte-identical vector it was scored with under gate-set v3. One cached query -- 'what does article 257 of the Swiss Code of Obligations say about rent' -- matches no row in any scored set and predates this amendment; task 602 found it, reported it, and did not remove it.
1418.gate_set_version_why: The cache digest pins the query VECTORS. It cannot see the row set, and the row set is what ADR-107 amendment 3 moved: an arm scored on the 1,396 rows and an arm scored on the 1,420 rows both carry cache digest bd5e59e3... and both report cache_miss = 0, so without this pin the instrument-integrity clause would accept the two as an A/B (verification-doctrine 3). Every leg json gate_authority.py writes stamps its GATE_SET_VERSION, every seal carries it, and `flip_gate._instrument_problems` refuses an arm whose stamp is not this value or is missing. Moving this pin is a PR, like every other pin in this file.
1418.gate_set_version_pin_history: v3 (tasks 531/542; the set every 584 / 591 / 594 arm was scored on) -> v4 (task 602, ADR-107 amendment 3: the 24 contaminated rows removed, 1,420 -> 1,396 rows). Arms sealed under v3 stay valid history under v3; they are refused as evidence for a flip judged under v4.
1418.note: Held out from tuning (task 519 §6.4: the levers were measured on it as a DIAGNOSTIC, never fitted to it). The instrument is the pinned query-vector cache, not a tracked file: it is 1,418 embedded vectors built once on GPU, and both legs read it so the A/B delta is the lever and not embedding noise. Pinned here by its sha256, which every arm seal carries.

contamination.finding: 24 of the 199 entries in `data/refresh_manifest.json` carry an `eval_id`, and all 24 name a real query in THIS held-out set -- every one `intent=freshness`, in the `authoritative` sub-set. Task 106 wrote them 'one per failing freshness query', maintained 'content currency by editing the manifest's text', and recorded at the time that switching to real fetched HTML made the score WORSE ('naive raw-HTML re-extraction dilutes the curated passage text and regressed freshness dom@10 1.00 -> 0.97, hit@1 0.79 -> 0.72'). That is teaching-to-the-test: measured, preferred, and documented at the time. Tasks 107b and 148 wrote the other 175 entries under a stated no-eval-file firewall, so their overlap with the gold set is empirical, not targeted -- the two must not be flattened into one story. 24/24 match the query's `gold_domains`; 5/24 also match `gold_urls` exactly; 0 of the 24 are in the 629 v2 chooser.

contamination.disposition_note: RULED AND EXECUTED 2026-09-17. The 24 queries have left data/eval_authoritative.yaml. The timing this item recommended when it was opened was honoured: the contamination flattered the INCUMBENT -- production carried all 370 authored rows and aw_e8 carries 0 -- so the queries stayed in for the flip battery, which held the candidate to the harder bar, and they leave after it. Consequence, stated rather than worked around: every arm sealed under gate-set v3 (tasks 584, 591, 594 and data/flip-gate-verdict.v1.json) was scored on the contaminated set. Those seals remain valid history under the version they name; this gate refuses them as evidence for a flip judged under v4, because two arms scored on two row sets are not an A/B. The next battery is re-run on the 1,396-row set, against the same pinned query cache, and re-sealed.

They are excluded from it BY NAME rather than by a `mrr is null` heuristic — a rule that silently skips whatever it cannot parse is how a class stops being checked.

regression_free.rule: For every leg, every instrument and every class with golds, the candidate's h@1, h@10 and MRR must be >= the incumbent's. A single class losing on a single leg refuses the flip unless a named ruling covers exactly that (leg, instrument, class, metric). Amended by Ruling 31 (Tim 2026-10-12), ADR-043 A10: this rule binds the legs in `strict_legs`; the component legs are read by `component_arms` (informational), and an `accepted_losses` entry can cover a strict cell.
regression_free.tolerance_why: ADR-043's ranking/serving bar is per-gold zero-loss: there, one regressed gold is a real defect. A flip is the largest ranking change this system makes, so it meets the strict bar, not the content bar's net-non-negative one.
regression_free.mrr_epsilon_why: MRR is reported rounded to 4 decimals in every sealed arm, so a difference smaller than half of the last published digit is a rounding artifact, not a measurement. Counts have no such epsilon.
regression_free.strict_legs_why: Ruling 31 (Tim 2026-10-12, plan.md T21 option (c)): the FULL STACK is what a user gets and stays under the strict bar above, per class, tolerance 0. The component legs (dense-only, sparse-only) are read by `component_arms` instead. A contract without this key is the contract before ruling 31 (every leg strict), and the gate reads it that way.

component_arms.ruled_via: chat 2026-10-12 15:50Z, 'OK, you can do everything as recommended' -- executes plan.md T21's recommendation: '(c) for the component arms'
component_arms.why: Task 863 measured two NULL pairs on 1.9M-row component arms -- a rebuild null (the same rows built twice) and an id null (the same rows under other ids, i.e. another HNSW graph). Each moves one gold, or one reciprocal rank, in single classes: rebuild null ch-stats-010 (held-out full-stack authoritative h@10 -1) and ho-fr-009 (held-out sparse-only freshness h@10 -1); id null en14 rank 1 -> 2 (629 entity and held-out dom_entity, h@1 -1 / MRR -1.0, full-stack and dense-only). A zero-tolerance bar applied to a component arm on its own therefore flags the instrument, not the change. The component arms stay REQUIRED (`required_arms`) and keep every integrity clause (`arm_integrity`); they lose only the power to refuse.
component_arms.rule: A component cell (instrument x component leg x class x metric) whose candidate is below the incumbent is FLAGGED only when it is worse than BOTH null pairs' cells of the same instrument x leg x class by more than the nulls' own spread: flagged <=> d < min(0, d_null_a, d_null_b) - spread - eps. Units are GOLD UNITS: h@1 and h@10 as gold counts, MRR as the reciprocal-rank SUM (the class's mean MRR x its gold count). `spread` = the largest |d| either null pair shows in ANY class of the same instrument x leg x metric (which class a null's noisy gold lands in is chance). `eps` = mrr_epsilon x the class's gold count for MRR, 0 for counts. The 0 inside the min makes the reading one-sided, as ADR-043 A3 rule 4: a null that GAINED is noise, not a raised bar.
component_arms.flag_means: Informational. A flag refuses nothing: every losing component cell, flagged or not, is printed and sealed in the verdict's `component_readings` with its nulls, spread and bar, and the flagged cells are named in the report to Tim. A flagged cell is a ranking item (e.g. ADR-043 A1's eviction by volume), never a waiver.
component_arms.null_pairs: Two null pairs per component instrument x leg, supplied to the gate as pairs of sealed arms of that instrument x leg (`--null-pair NAME:KIND:INSTRUMENT:LEG=A,B`; the gate computes B - A itself). Each arm of a pair meets the instrument clauses of a battery arm (pinned digest, gate-set version, n_errors = 0); a pair that does not is reported in `null_pair_notes` and not used. A cell with fewer than two usable null readings is FLAGGED with that reason: an unread cell is reported, never silently passed.
component_arms.null_pair_kinds_why: Closed list (ADR-043 A3 rule 6). rebuild = the same rows built twice by the same code (task 863 e1null); id = the same rows under another id set, i.e. another HNSW graph (task 863 e1idnull); reread = one physical state read twice in the same hours (spec specs/aw-e10-rebuild.md section 5 (c): each side of the flip battery is read twice). A new way of producing a null is an ADR change.

regression_free.accepted_losses_rule: A strict cell that loses is COVERED when every accepted loss naming it (same instrument, leg, class, and the candidate collection when the entry names one) applies, and the class's loss with those golds' own rank changes removed clears the strict bar (>= 0 for counts, >= -mrr_epsilon x gold count for the MRR sum). An entry applies only when both arms carry per-gold ranks for the class (run_arm rows, or the held-out leg json pinned by the seal's leg_sha256) and the gold ranks no lower on the candidate than `shown.candidate_rank`: a re-run where it falls further is a fresh refusal. A covered cell is printed and sealed with its raw numbers in `regressions` and `accepted`, and `measured_verdict` stays FAIL. An entry is Tim's, by ruling, by PR (memory: gate-waivers-escalate-to-tim); a builder or gate-runner never adds one.

noise_floor.status: PROPOSED -- ADR-107 amendment 2, Option 2. Inert while `enabled` is false: `flip_gate.noise_allowance` returns 0.0 and no verdict changes. Enabling it is a one-line legislative change, Tim's, by PR.
noise_floor.rule: When enabled, a named ruling covers a cell while the measured loss is no worse than (the loss it was ruled over + this cell's `allowance`). Nothing else moves: the collection binding, the mandatory cite, the pending-evidence refusal, the arm and instrument clauses, latency and preservation are untouched, and every covered cell still prints and still seals with its raw numbers under `measured_verdict: FAIL`.
noise_floor.basis: Per cell, the movement measured between two seals of the SAME comparison (twin vs aw_e8, twelve arms, same pinned instruments) on collections that were not written between them -- task 584 flip-gate-verdict.v1.json and data/flip-gate-verdict.v1.json. A cell qualifies only if it lost in BOTH seals: a cell that did not lose before has no re-run pair, and a cell that STARTS losing is the thing the gate exists to catch.
noise_floor.derivation: tasks/592-scripts/build_named_ruling_592.py --noise. pipeline/test_flip_gate.py re-derives `cells` from the two sealed verdicts.
noise_floor.weakness: Two observations, one instrument. The allowance covers the 10 cells that refused on 2026-09-16 BY CONSTRUCTION, because it was measured on exactly those cells: it describes the second run, it does not predict a third. It is also not a fix. The instrument's non-reproducibility is already a post-flip obligation on this ruling, and the cure is a battery that reproduces, not a gate that tolerates.
would_not_cover: any cell whose loss grows beyond (ruled loss + allowance) -- still a refusal, still named, still Tim's
any cell with no named ruling at all: the floor widens coverage, it never creates it
the 3 cells that started losing in the 591 seal -- they had no ruled loss to widen, which is why re-binding, not the floor, is what covers them
any non-regression clause: missing arms, a moved instrument digest, n_errors, cache_miss, both sides on one collection, latency over prod's deadline, the preservation tiers
noise_floor.counterfactual: Had this floor been in force on the ORIGINAL 584 bound, task 591 would have refused on 4 problems, not 14: the 10 exceeded cells covered, the 3 new class losses still refused, the preservation clause still refused. The floor alone would not have saved that battery; the re-bind is what does the work.

regression_free.named_rulings_note: ONE ruling, Tim's, 2026-09-16 (task 590) -- it was empty until then. Two shapes are accepted. The original per-cell shape is {leg, instrument, class, metric, ruling, cite} and covers exactly one cell. Task 590's shape carries an `id` and an `overrides` LIST under one ruling, because Tim ruled once, on one battery, over 87 cells at a time: writing that as 87 unrelated waivers would lose the fact that they are one decision and would leave 86 standing if the 87th were withdrawn. Either shape must `cite` a ruling that exists -- a waiver is Tim's, by PR (memory: gate-waivers-escalate-to-tim); nothing here may be added by a builder or a gate-runner. An `overrides` entry that carries its incumbent/candidate pair binds the ruling to the loss it was SHOWN: pipeline/flip_gate.py covers the cell only while the measured delta is no worse than the ruled one, refuses when a ruling's `candidate_collection` is not the collection the candidate arms scored, and (via assert_sealed_pass) refuses the flip itself while any `pending_evidence` entry on an applied ruling has not landed. The ruling moves the VERDICT LINE only: every overridden cell still prints and still seals with its raw numbers, and the seal carries `measured_verdict: FAIL`.

arm_integrity.one_instrument: Every arm on an instrument must carry the same instrument digest. Two arms scored against different query sets are not an A/B (verification-doctrine 3, `the experiment is the flag`).
arm_integrity.no_errors: An arm with n_errors > 0 is refused, not averaged over. An error is not an empty (verification-doctrine 6); a leg that timed out on 40 queries scores like a leg that answered them wrongly.
arm_integrity.cache_miss_zero: A 1,418 arm must report cache_miss = 0. A miss means that query was embedded by something other than the pinned cache, so the two legs no longer share vectors.
arm_integrity.distinct_sides: The incumbent and candidate arms must name different collections. Task 447: from 2026-08-16 to 2026-08-27 `heimdall:6334` was an SSH tunnel to production while the twin was empty, and a `url != url` check could not see it (ADR-098 Ruling 3).

latency.source_why: Prod's own deadline, read from the file the monitor reads, so the gate and the alarm can never disagree about what 'too slow' means (engineering-doctrine 2).
latency.storage_why: The candidate must be measured on the storage it will serve from. Task 518 measured a live restore degrading prod's /search from ~0.2 s to ~3.5 s -- a page-cache effect, entirely a property of where the bytes are.
latency.measured_note: Task 524 measured the candidate full-stack at p50 529 ms / p95 763 ms and the dense-only candidate at p95 1935 ms, both on NVMe.

tier2.scope_amended_by: ADR-107 amendment 2 (task 592) -- PENDING Tim's merge. Before it, this clause applied to a flip too.
tier2.scope_basis: ADR-098 Ruling 1 writes one preservation law per operation class. The incremental tier -- what pipeline/content_pack_preservation.py implements -- is 'a twin-first apply of an incremental content pack'. The rebuild tier is 'any full rebuild, ship+flip, or promotion', and Ruling 1 gates it with the sealed GLOBAL preservation manifest instead. A flip is the second kind. Demanding the first of it was the wrong law for the operation, which is why no flip battery in the record has ever satisfied it: tasks/{533,576,584}-artifacts/flip-gate-verdict*.json and data/flip-gate-verdict.v1.json all carry it in `problems` (task 591 §5.3).
tier2.rule: A sealed tier-2 contract PASS must be presented for an incremental content-pack apply. A failing source is excluded by REGENERATING the pack without it, never waived (ADR-098 Ruling 2).
tier2.not_evidence_for_a_flip: The only sealed content-pack PASS this repo has produced is task 452's `task452-news-20260828`. The pack it authorized was never applied -- its own ADR-043 content gate failed it on 2026-08-29, 227 -> 222 h@1 with 29 strict per-gold losses. It says nothing about aw_e8 and is not presented as if it did.
tier2.twin_distinctness: ADR-098 Ruling 3: the preflight must prove twin and production are physically different Qdrant instances -- instance/peer identity, not URL strings.

rebuild_tier.adr: ADR-098 Ruling 1 -- the rebuild/promotion tier. Unchanged by that ADR ('nothing in this ADR weakens data/production-rebuild-lock.v1.json or its five gaps') and unchanged by ADR-107 am.2, which only moves the flip under the correct one of the two laws.
rebuild_tier.manifest_why: The DEFAULT, and what governs every candidate NOT named in `candidate_manifests`. It is `blocked`, for aw_e3, with five open gaps, and it refuses.
rebuild_tier.candidate_manifests_why: ADR-098 amendment 1. A named ruling is bound to ONE collection, so the manifest carrying it is bound to one collection too. `flip_gate._rebuild_tier_manifest` resolves the candidate's own entry first and falls back to `manifest`, so a ruling granted for the aw_e8 flip can never quietly become the preservation basis for the next one: every other candidate still meets the blocked global manifest.
rebuild_tier.rule: A ship+flip requires a global preservation manifest that is `status: sealed` and names the candidate collection. `flip_gate._preservation_problems` checks those two facts at the front of the process and fails closed on a missing, unreadable, unsealed or mis-addressed manifest.
rebuild_tier.enforced_again_at: pipeline/promote/alias_swap.sh, for alias aw_prod: `python3 pipeline/preservation_contract.py verify --manifest <file> --expect-collection <candidate> --artifact-root $AW_ARTIFACT_ROOT --deep`, exit 3 on anything but PASS. That is the DEEP check -- five profile stages, count-conserving lineage, content-fidelity, off-box durability receipts -- and it runs at the alias swap whatever this gate says. `verify_manifest` raises unless `status == 'sealed'` and `collection.name` equals the candidate.
rebuild_tier.why_here_too: deployment-doctrine: a cheap check at the front of an expensive process. A flip refused at the alias swap is refused at 06:00 with the overlay already shipped; the same refusal from the battery costs nothing.
rebuild_tier.ruled_status: ADR-098 amendment 1 adds `status: ruled` to aw.preservation-manifest.v1: a status that can be granted only by writing down what is still owed. This gate accepts it only when the manifest carries a `ruling` block, that block names a `ratified_by`, and it covers THIS candidate. It does not re-adjudicate the ruling. `preservation_contract.verify_manifest` checks the carried gaps, the rollback target and the reconciled membership receipts DEEPLY at the alias swap, refuses a ruled manifest verified without an --expect-collection, and prints the open obligations to stderr on every verify.
rebuild_tier.state_2026_09_16: SATISFIED for aw_e8 by a NAMED RULING, not by a proof. data/production-flip-ruling-aw_e8.v1.json is `status: ruled`: the collection identity, the point count (33,723,480), an off-box membership receipt, the aw_e3 rollback target with its own receipt, and the destructive step withheld are all proven and deep-verified; the five gaps G2/G3/G6/G8/G9 are CARRIED by name as post-flip obligations, each with an owner and a vehicle. data/production-rebuild-lock.v1.json is untouched -- still `blocked`, still five open gaps, still aw_e3 -- and still governs every other candidate. Until 2026-09-16 this field read: "UNSATISFIED for aw_e8. The only aw.preservation-manifest.v1 document in the repo is data/production-rebuild-lock.v1.json: `status: blocked`, five open gaps (G2/G3/G6/G8/G9), collection `aw_e3`, 34,464,401 points. No pipeline writes one -- it is hand-maintained. So scoping tier-2 correctly does NOT unblock the flip: it replaces a clause that was the wrong law with the right one, which also refuses, and which alias_swap.sh would have refused on anyway. Lifting it is a separate ruling and is not drafted here." Drafting that ruling is what task 593 did.
rebuild_tier.not_rechecked_at_assert_pass: `assert_sealed_pass` re-checks the fusion-weights pointer and the named rulings against the contract in force, and deliberately does NOT re-check this manifest: alias_swap.sh verifies it deeply at the swap itself, seconds before the alias moves, which is a stronger position than re-reading it here.

seal.rule: verify_flip_config refuses a flip whose sealed verdict is absent, not PASS, not for the serving config being verified, or not derived from the arms it names (each arm re-digested at seal time and again at verify time).
seal.expiry_note: A verdict is bound to the candidate collection name and the arm digests. Re-staging the candidate invalidates it, because the arms no longer describe the collection that would be served.
